$comment: Gzipped KB budgets enforced by scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs in CI.
'initial-load' is the headline: the entry script, every modulepreload hint,
and the stylesheet — what a first-time visitor downloads before the app is
usable. After code splitting (TD-004) it is the only size number that still
tracks user experience. Total bundle size went UP when splitting landed,
because chunking adds module overhead, while the page got ~6x faster to start.
Budgets are ratchets set just above today's measurement. 'current' is the last
measured value, refreshed with --update, so the report can show a delta.

initial-load.label: Initial load (entry + preloads + CSS)
initial-load.why: What the user waits for. 1252 KB before code splitting (TD-004), 199.3 KB after, then 85.9 KB once ADR-0005 deleted Firebase — vendor-firebase was ~113 KB gzipped of it, larger than React. Ratcheted 230 -> 110 so that saving cannot quietly be spent.

largest-js-chunk.label: Largest single JS chunk
largest-js-chunk.why: Now a lazy vendor chunk (spreadsheet libs), not the entry — it costs only the tools that use it. Kept as a guard against one lazy chunk quietly becoming enormous.

total-js.label: Total JavaScript (all chunks)
total-js.why: Expected to exceed the pre-split total: splitting duplicates some module overhead. Ratcheted 1600 -> 1450 after ADR-0005 removed Firebase (-101.8 KB). Headroom is deliberate: one new lazy tab should not fail the gate, because a gate that fails routinely gets bypassed. Watched for runaway growth, not optimised down.
